proof_summary: For \(k\ge 60\), set \(n=2k+1\); any nonzero matrix entry yields primes \(n+i-j\) and \(n+j-i\) whose sum is \(2n=4k+2\), so if no such decomposition existed the entire matrix would be zero, contradicting its nonzero determinant. The remaining cases \(1\le k<60\) are settled by explicit prime decompositions.
